name: Cessna 120/140
summary: Postwar two-seat tailwheel high-wing from Cessna: a simple, affordable sport and training airplane that predates the tricycle-gear Cessna 150.

wings: High wing braced by V-struts (120/140) or a single strut per side (140A)
Constant-chord wing; fabric-covered on 120/140, metal on 140A
engines: Single small flat-four in a neat, round cowling
fuselage: Two-seat cabin with one door per side
Fixed spring-steel main gear with a tailwheel
Rear quarter windows on the 140 (absent on most 120s)
tail: Rounded fin and rudder with a low horizontal tail

tellTales: Small two-seat strut-braced high-wing on a tailwheel
Flat spring-steel main gear legs under a compact, boxy cabin
Rounded fin and rudder on a compact tail

confusedWith.howToTell: The 120/140 has flat spring-steel gear legs and Cessna's squarer lines; the Luscombe 8 has short oleo-style struts with exposed rubber cord and an all-metal, rounder fuselage.
The 120/140 has a tailwheel and a nose-high stance; the 150 sits on tricycle gear.
The 140 has a side-by-side cabin with a metal fuselage and spring-steel gear; the Champ is tandem seating with a fabric fuselage and a distinct long, narrow cabin.
The 120/140 is a short two-seater; the 170 is longer with a bigger four-seat cabin.
